messages:
sarah: noticing a recurring tail-latency spike when the continuous-batcher switches from steady coalesce -> flush. happens mostly on mixed short/long requests, and tenants with bursty small requests are starving others. any quick theories?

dmitri: sounds like headroom exhaustion + a bad eviction order. small requests keep getting packed then evicted when a long request forces a flush. we probably need stronger isolation or smarter flush signals.

sarah: yep. i sketched two options: 1) per-tenant micro-queues plus an opportunistic central coalescer that pulls from micro-queues by priority; 2) keep shared queue but add soft-quotas (credit buckets) + preemptive flush hooks that target oldest cohorts first.

lee: option 1 buys isolation but complicates KV cache locality and batching efficiency. if micro-queues are too small we lose coalescing gains.

dmitri: option 2 is lower-risk but we need a clean admission API and an eviction policy aware of KV cache affinity. otherwise we flip-flop and still hit long-tail.

ana: (typo) -> ana: adding: remember memory for KV cache is per-GPU. moving to micro-queues might increase overall memory pressure unless we coordinate cache share or make per-queue cache hints.

sarah: good note. one variant: keep shared memory for KV cache, but tag queue entries with cache-fingerprint so coalescer prefers entries with overlapping prefixes. that preserves batching while giving micro-queues logical isolation.

lee: that could work. another angle: tokenized soft-credits where each tenant has a circulating token budget. when budget < threshold we throttle admission instead of evicting in-flight batches. tokens refill at a rate tuned to SLA.

sarah: pseudo:
```
if tenant_tokens[tid] < MIN_HEADROOM:
  delay(admit) or route to fallback
else:
  admit and decrement tokens
```
we'd add hysteresis to avoid oscillation.

dmitri: love the token idea for short requests. for long-generation heavy tenants we need a separate path: long-gens should prefer dedicated lanes (or limited concurrency) so they don't monopolize the coalescer. maybe a fastpath flag on request metadata.

ana -> ana: telemetry question: what metrics do we need to know success? i propose: per-tenant avg coalesce window, preemptive-flush-counts, kv-cache-hit-by-cohort, admit-throttle-events, and queue-starvation-duration.

ana: ops-bot: posted an alert earlier about a 95th p99 jump at 4109876001. re-checking traces now.

ops-bot: deploy: continuous-batcher/patch-2026-03-18 rolled to canary on gpus-us-west-2 (id: cb-2026-03-18). no errors in logs.

lee: migration plan idea: implement token-buckets + telemetry first as non-invasive layer on top of current shared queue. run canary, watch kv-cache-hit and p99. if token-buckets reduce starved victims but hurt throughput, iterate to micro-queues + coalescer in phase 2.

sarah: agreed. action items: 1) dmitri + lee to prototype token-bucket admission shim (2 days), 2) ana to add the telemetry hooks (metrics + a small trace tag) (1 day), 3) ops to run canary and collect 48h of traffic. meet in 72h to evaluate.

dmitri: will open a quick PR with the admission API and a draft config for per-tenant refill rates.

lee: i'll prototype token leak algorithm and a simple sim to eyeball throughput vs p99 tradeoffs.

ana -> ana: i'll make the dashboard panels and add a dashboard link in thread once ready. :thumbsup:

sarah: thanks everyone. trying to keep changes minimal so we can iterate without redoing runtime kernels. :rocket:
